text:
Trevor: TL;DR: proposal for a verifier-sidecar resume protocol + tiny manifest contract to make airgapped onprem upgrades resumable without manual intervention. problem we keep hitting: partial applies during flaky media transfers or operator crashes and ops has to ssh in every time.

Asha: big yes to reducing manual recovery. what's the minimal contract look like?

Trevor: minimal pieces: ordered component list, per-component activation sequence number, content hash, and an append-only apply-checkpoint log path. plus a short activation lease to prevent races. sidecar takes over only when lease absent/expired and checkpoint is consistent.

Jin: activation lease = how long? who grants it? what if operator renews mid-reboot?

Trevor: operator acquires lease (owner id + ttl) before starting apply. TTL default 60s, operator renews periodically. if node reboots or process dies lease lapses and sidecar may attempt resume. sidecar must validate checkpoint matches manifest hashes before touching state.

Maya: we need event types for observability so console can show exactly why a resume happened. suggested events: manifest.fetched, lease.acquired, lease.expired, apply.started, apply.component.succeeded, apply.component.failed, verify.resume.attempt, verify.resume.success, verify.resume.abort.

ops: can sidecar and operator race on the same component? e.g., operator is applying component X and sidecar thinks lease expired due to small clock skew.

Trevor: mitigate with two steps: 1) short grace window where sidecar verifies lease expiry using monotonic clock + tries a one-shot lease-claim handshake (compare-and-swap), 2) components must be idempotent or provide a safe-precheck hook. manifest includes apply_idempotent boolean and optional precheck_cmd for author-specified safety checks.

Jin: how do we prevent confused-deputy when manifests are fetched from untrusted media? signing?

Trevor: manifest and checkpoints signed by operator keypair. support KMS-backed signing if available; on fully airgapped installs default to locally provisioned operator key with clear rotation instructions. sidecar only accepts signed manifests matching a configured trust anchor.

Maya: payloads for events should be structured JSON so console ingestion and search is easy. example event: {"ts":"2026-07-05T09:22:11Z","host":"node-3","event":"verify.resume.success","component":"model-store","seq":12,"reason":"lease-expired"} (we'll ship as newline-delimited JSON).

Asha: what about mismatch during resume? e.g., checkpoint says component applied but blob hash now differs (corruption).

Trevor: default behavior: abort resume and emit verify.resume.abort with failure reason. recommend an operator-visible remediation hint: "blob-corrupt -> run media-check or restore from artifact-store". advanced flows can try mirror-repair if configured but these must also emit events and be opt-in. no silent repairs.

ops: storage for checkpoints: where and how durable? we need something that survives abrupt power loss reliably.

Trevor: append-only WAL with atomic fsync per entry + periodic compacted snapshot. keep last-good manifest copy next to checkpoint. path configurable (default /var/lib/redwood/upgrade-checkpoint). replayable format so agent can reconstruct apply position after boot.

Jin: API surface for agent/sidecar? sketch please.

Trevor: small HTTP-ish local API (or unix-socket) to keep things simple: GET /manifest/:id -> manifest.json, POST /checkpoint {component_id, seq, hash, signer}, POST /lease {holder_id, ttl}, POST /lease/renew, POST /lease/claim {holder_id, expected_rev}, POST /verify-action {action, reason, meta}. responses signed by operator in operator-mode.

Maya: also add a concise human-readable audit string for console display so SREs don't need to parse raw JSON. e.g., "resume: node-3 claimed lease after TTL expired; completed 2/5 components."

Asha: are we changing operator UX? need to show lease state in CLI too. operator should be able to yield lease if they want someone else (sidecar) to try recovery. maybe `redwood-upgrade yield-lease --manifest man-...`

Trevor: agree. CLI helpers: show-manifest, show-checkpoint, claim-lease, yield-lease, inject-failure (test).

deploy-bot: recorded: manifest="edge-service-v3" submitted by Trevor @1770024688 id=man-20260705-09 status=staged. :white_check_mark:

Jin: one more crypto note: signatures on checkpoints prevent a malicious node from forging progress. checkpoints should include manifest id, component id, seq, timestamp and be signed. sidecar validates consistency.

Maya: observability: dashboards: 1) cluster upgrade heatmap, 2) hosts with frequent lease expirations, 3) mismatch/failure trend. alert: >3 resume.abort events on a host in 30m -> page.

ops: rollback scenarios? if resume fails mid-way, do we auto-revert or leave system in degraded partial state?

Trevor: default: do not auto-revert. leave system in the last known consistent checkpoint and notify operator. reason: automatic revert can cause worse downtime in many cases. we can add optional auto-rollback policy as an explicit feature with safeguards.

Asha: next steps?

Trevor: I'll author an RFC with manifest schema, checkpoint WAL format, and the RPC proto. PoC plan: extend agent for checkpoint API + simple lease manager, plus console event ingestion for resume events. volunteers: Jin=signing & keyflow doc, Maya=event schema & dashboards, Asha=CLI/UX for lease and manual controls.

Jin: happy to pick signing work.

Maya: will prototype event schema.

Asha: will own CLI UX writeup.

Trevor: thanks folks. I'll open the RFC and link to this thread, plus include a short appendix with example manifests and sample WAL lines. :thumbsup:
